text: Debugging is an essential skill for every programmer. When a program does not work as expected, the first step is identifying bugs by observing the symptoms, such as error messages or unexpected results. Good debugging tools, like breakpoints and stack traces, help you find where the problem happens. However, a systematic approach matters most: form a hypothesis, test it, and change one thing at a time. Logging is also valuable, because well-placed log messages show what the program is doing and make it easier to reproduce the issue. By staying patient and organized, you can solve most bugs efficiently.
